newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebels say no talks Thursday on Congo soil.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say no talks Thursday on Congo soil.

text.p: Zaire rebels said there would be no talks with President Mobutu Sese Seko on Thursday if the location was Congo's Point Noire port and insisted talks be held in international waters.

"We are not going to have the talks in Point Noire and apparently Mr Mobutu doesn't want to go to the international waters so the talks will not talk place today (Wednesday) or tomorrow," rebel Justice "Commissioner-General" Mwenze Kongolo told Reuters by telephone.

"We are talking to the South Africans and there is no problem. The only thing we are requiring to do is go to a neutral place and we are still prepared to go," Kongolo said speaking from the Angolan enclave of Cabinda.
He said the rebel advance on Kinshasa was continuing despite the prospective talks, but gave no details.
On the subject matter of talks Kongolo said: "We came here to hear his (Mobutu's) answer to our proposals and they include his departure."
Rebels earlier argued Point Noire port was "enemy ground" and said Mobutu was healthy enough to travel on the South African ship to international waters.
South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said talks scheduled for Wednesday were postponed, probably until Thursday.
